Designed for simplicity, engineered for outcomes

 

The T2 Alpha Humerus Nailing System offers an innovative implant that may help to improve patients' lives, simplify humeral nail fixation for surgeons and streamline processes for hospital staff.

text_copy.text:
Advanced nail design
 

Stryker Orthopedic Modeling and Analytics (SOMA) designed1

  • Straight Nail design allows for alignment of the epiphyseal fragment with the diaphysis and gives structural support to the humeral head fragment8 
  • Proximal screw trajectories are designed to aim for dense bone to reduce the potential of displacement of the humeral head2,4 
  • Diameters defined through the SOMA database cover a wide range of intramedullary canal diameters in the analyzed population1

 

Active intraoperative compression  

  • Up to 6mm of controlled compression for long nails 
  • Designed to allow for a more controlled reduction of the fragments when compared to the traditional backslapping/backstroke method

Putting more options in your hands

  • Hybrid locking configuration designed for fixation of varying fracture patterns

text.text:
Stability when and where you need it


Advanced Locking Screws

  • Designed to provide increased axial fracture stability in any 4mm round locking hole when the surgeon chooses.6,7

PEEK insert

  • Designed to reduce potential for screw backout with locking screw or advanced locking screw in proximal holes9

Washers

  • Designed to increase surface area while reducing screw head prominence
  • Designed to improve bone fragment compression through increased surface area

Instrumentation made easy

Integrated instrument platform

  • One core basic tray is used for all T2 Alpha and Gamma4 indications, improving platform consistency and ease of use. 

Guided targeters

  • Targeters available for every hole except the distal lateral to medial hole
  • Distal targeting may potentially reduce radiation exposure and the time required for distal screw placement compared to perfect circles technique, as demonstrated in a comparable femur procedure5

Unique instrumentation 

  • Nail Height Stop: facilitates precise nail depth placement, while reducing the risk of nail protrusion through the proximal humerus.  
  • Cuff Spreading Device: designed to reduce the potential for rotator cuff damage
